26	
27	A full local copy of the HERE SDK API reference, docs, and examples is set up in `here-sdk_local_doc/`. Use it as the source of truth. Find what you need with plain shell:
28	
29	```sh
30	# locate the doc tree (don't assume the exact location)
31	find . -type d -name "here-sdk_local_doc"
32	
33	# find an API, class, or method
34	grep -rn "HERE.routing.RoutingEngine" here-sdk_local_doc/
35	grep -rni "bottom sheet" here-sdk_local_doc/
36	
37	# find an example or asset to reuse
38	grep -rln "MapMarker" here-sdk_local_doc/
39	find here-sdk_local_doc/ -name "*.png" -o -name "*.svg"
40	```
41	
42	Read the local doc or example before calling any HERE API. If it isn't in `here-sdk_local_doc/`, say so — don't invent it.
43	
44	## HERE SDK — use the SDK, never reinvent it
45	
46	**If HERE SDK provides it, use it. Never build a custom version.**
47	
48	Before writing any navigation, routing, mapping, or location code, check whether the SDK already does it. The SDK covers:
49	
50	- **Location smoothing / interpolation** — `VisualNavigator.startRendering()` handles it. Do not write custom interpolation between GPS pings.
51	- **Camera follow** — `DynamicCameraBehavior()` / `FixedCameraBehavior()`. Do not hand-animate the camera.
52	- **Autosuggest / geocoding** — `SearchEngine`. Do not call a third-party geocoder or write a custom debounce layer around a raw HTTP search API.

56	- **Turn-by-turn instructions** — `ManeuverNotificationListener` / route-progress listener provides text and distance. Do not compute instructions from raw geometry.
57	- **Speed-limit warnings** — `SpeedWarningListener`. Do not derive speed limits from raw map data.

59	
60	The rule: **grep the local package source (`packages/here_sdk/lib/`) and docs (`here-sdk_doc_local/`) first. If the capability exists there, use it. Only write custom code for things the SDK genuinely does not provide.**
61	
62	## Engineering Standard
63	
64	Write boring code only. Boring means: clear names, small files, small widgets, simple control flow, predictable state, obvious folder structure. No magic abstractions, no clever one-liners, no unnecessary packages, no framework cosplay, no sci-fi architecture names.
65	
66	Clever code is technical debt with a short fuse. Readable code wins.
67	
68	Change only what was asked. Don't refactor adjacent code you weren't pointed at. Don't add docstrings, type annotations, or comments to lines you didn't touch. Don't add defensive handling for cases that can't happen. Don't introduce an abstraction for one call site. If an adjacent problem surfaces while fixing the asked-for one, name it in one line — don't fix it silently.
69	
70	## Product Standard
71	
72	The app must feel simple, fast, and human. Every change preserves or improves startup, responsiveness, scroll, readability, accessibility, localization readiness, and maintainability.
73	
74	No technical jargon in user-facing text.
75	
76	Bad → Good:
77	
78	```txt
79	Failed to mutate entity   → Could not save your changes. Please try again.
80	Auth token expired        → Your session expired. Please sign in again.
81	Invalid payload           → Please check the highlighted fields.
82	Something went wrong       → Could not update your profile. Check your connection and try again.
83	```
84	
85	## Performance Standard
86	
87	Assume this runs on low-end Android (Samsung J2-class). Target 60 FPS where reasonable.
88	
89	Optimize only where code clearly risks jank, rebuild waste, leaks, slow startup, or wasted work. Don't optimize blindly. The recurring offenders:
90	
91	- Heavy work, async calls, or expensive object creation inside `build()`.
92	- Rebuilding a whole screen for one small state change. Missing `const`.
93	- Large collections without `ListView.builder` / `GridView.builder` / slivers.
94	- Undisposed controllers, focus nodes, streams, animation controllers, listeners, timers, subscriptions.
95	- Un-debounced expensive input handlers.
96	- Unsized/uncached large images; gratuitous opacity, blur, shadow, shader, clipping, or animation.
97	- Blocking the first frame with avoidable work.
98	
99	## Flutter & State Standards
100	
101	Follow the project's existing conventions. Prefer official Flutter/Dart patterns over custom abstractions. Use the state management already in the project — do not introduce Riverpod, Bloc, Provider, GetX, MobX, Redux, a custom event bus, or any new dependency unless the user approves it. Don't upgrade dependencies. Don't rewrite working architecture because you'd have done it differently.
102	
103	State must be explicit, inspectable, and safe across async and after disposal. Guard async UI updates:
104	
105	```dart
106	if (!context.mounted) return;
107	```
108	
109	## Folder Structure
110	
111	Keep it boring and predictable. Follow whatever the project already uses — feature-first if that's the pattern, simple flat structure if that's the pattern. Consistency beats theory.
112	
113	Feature-first reference (use only the layers that exist or are genuinely needed):
114	
115	```txt
116	feature_name/
117	  data/        models/ repositories/ sources/
118	  domain/      entities/ use_cases/
119	  presentation/screens/ widgets/ controllers/
120	  l10n/
121	  feature_name.dart
122	```
123	
124	Simple reference:
125	
126	```txt
127	profile/
128	  profile_screen.dart
129	  profile_controller.dart
130	  profile_repository.dart
131	  widgets/ profile_header.dart profile_form.dart
132	```
133	
134	Don't create empty folders, fake architecture, gratuitous file splits, or barrels the project doesn't already use.
135	
136	## Naming
137	
138	Clear, boring, searchable. Names explain purpose, not implementation trivia.
139	
140	Good: `userProfile`, `saveButton`, `isSubmitting`, `loadOrders`, `paymentRepository`, `ProfileHeader`
141	Bad: `data`, `tmp`, `res`, `managerThing`, `handlerX`, `UltraProfileEngine`, `SmartFormOrchestrator`
142	
143	- Widget file name matches the main exported widget.
144	- Class names describe their actual role; boolean names read like true/false statements; async method names describe the action.
145	- Avoid abbreviations unless standard in the project. Avoid `Helper`/`Manager`/`Service`/`Utils` unless the project already uses them consistently.
146	- No collisions with model fields, API fields, or DB columns. Magic numbers get named constants.
147	
148	## Widgets
149	
150	A screen file mostly composes smaller widgets. A widget has one job.
151	
152	Avoid: 300-line screen files, business logic in `build()`, large nested ternaries, repeated padding/layout/loading/error/empty markup, anonymous widgets that should be extracted, stateful widgets where stateless suffices.
153	
154	Prefer: extracted private widgets for local-only UI, reusable public widgets only when actually reused, and clear loading / success / failure / empty / disabled states on every interactive flow.
155	
156	## Localization
157	
158	All user-facing strings must be localizable — labels, titles, placeholders, helper text, validation messages, snack bars, dialogs, bottom sheets, errors, empty states, tooltips, accessibility labels. No hardcoded user-visible text in widgets.
159	
160	Use the project's existing system (`AppLocalizations.of(context)`, `context.l10n`, `S.of(context)`, whatever it is). Don't invent a new one.
161	
162	If Arabic is required but unavailable, use a placeholder — never invent translations:
163	
164	```txt
165	[ar] English text here
166	```
167	
168	## Error Handling
169	
170	Never swallow errors. No empty `catch`. Never show raw exception/server/DB/token/stack-trace text to users. Log developer context where the project has logging; show sanitized human messages. Errors carry enough context to debug at 3 AM.
171	
172	```dart
173	catch (error, stackTrace) {
174	  logger.error('Failed to load profile', error: error, stackTrace: stackTrace);
175	  state = const ProfileState.error(ProfileError.loadFailed);
176	}
177	```
178	
179	Match the project's logging and state patterns.
180	
181	## Validation
182	
183	Validate user input before submission — required fields, and email/phone/numeric/date/selection where applicable. Don't trust client input. Show all relevant field errors at once. Keep messages localizable and validation logic out of large widget trees. Reuse existing validators. No new validation package without approval.
184	
185	## Security
186	
187	Don't weaken security.
188	
189	- No secrets in the client. No logging tokens, passwords, OTPs, private IDs, or sensitive data.
190	- Don't pass sensitive tokens through routes unless that's already project convention.
191	- Validate route params, deep links, and external URLs before launching.
192	- Check permissions before showing or running privileged actions.
193	- Don't bypass or modify auth flows beyond safe null checks without approval.
194	
195	## Data Flow
196	
197	UI renders data; business logic lives outside widgets. Follow the project's equivalent of:
198	
199	```txt
200	screen → controller/state → repository → data source
201	```
202	
203	Screens don't hold complex API logic. Widgets receive data via parameters. Repositories hide data-source details. Models parse safely. Don't mix navigation, API calls, formatting, and validation in one widget. No duplicate fetch logic across screens.
204	
205	## Navigation
206	
207	Use the router pattern the project already uses — don't introduce a new one. Validate route arguments and deep-link inputs. Don't pass large objects or sensitive values through routes. Give a user-friendly fallback for missing/invalid route data.
208	
209	## Platform & Accessibility
210	
211	Targets iOS and Android. Avoid platform-specific behavior unless needed; when needed, isolate it, keep safe fallbacks, follow existing patterns, break neither platform. Handle denied and permanently-denied permissions clearly.
212	
213	Accessibility basics: reasonably sized tap targets, semantic labels on icon-only buttons, labels or explicit decorative marking on meaningful images, readable text at large font sizes, never color alone to convey meaning, clearly identified invalid fields.
214	
215	## Research
216	
217	Trust official sources, not memory. Before using or changing an API, verify from primary sources: Flutter/Dart docs, package docs, changelogs, source code, Apple/Android platform docs — and for HERE, the local `here-sdk_local_doc/` tree. Avoid SEO tutorials, random blogs, outdated StackOverflow. Don't claim an API behaves a certain way unless verified or already proven in the codebase.
218	
219	## Scope
220	
221	Fix only: folder structure, naming consistency, localization gaps, error UX, validation/safe data handling, performance risks, widget readability, platform correctness, accessibility basics. Nothing else.
222	
223	**Out of scope without approval:** new features/screens, visual redesigns, dependency upgrades or replacements, architecture/auth rewrites, backend/DB/API-contract changes, analytics, payment logic, release signing, CI/CD, generated files, native iOS/Android project files (unless the requested folder *is* native code), test rewrites (unless your scoped change breaks an existing test).
224	
225	Notice something important but out of scope? List it under `Out of scope but noticed`.
226	
227	## Workflow
228	
229	Do every step in order. Don't skip.
230	
231	**1. Ask for target.** Exact wording: `Which folder or feature should I clean up?` Wait for the answer.
232	
233	**2. Inventory.** List every file under the target. Tag which scope categories apply to each. Mark files to leave untouched and outside files needed as read-only context. No edits before the inventory is done.
234	
235	**3. Read context.** Learn the project's localization, routing, state, error-handling, logging, repository/data-source, model-parsing, folder-naming, and loading/error/empty patterns. Read 2–3 files that already do it right and match them. Don't invent your own.
236	
237	**4. Plan.** A focused checklist grouped by category (Localization / Error UX / Validation / Performance / Widget cleanup / Naming / Folder structure / Accessibility). Only real, applicable items. No broad refactors.
238	
239	**5. Fix in dependency order.** localization → models/validators → repositories/sources → controllers/state → screens → widgets → navigation glue → platform code (only if needed). After each edit, mentally check imports, null safety, names, l10n keys, rebuild behavior, disposal, and that it compiles.
240	
241	**6. Performance review.** Re-scan changed UI for the offenders in the Performance Standard. Fix only clear in-scope issues.
242	
243	**7. Verify.** Detect the project's commands. At minimum run `flutter analyze`. Run `flutter test` if tests exist and it's practical, and the lightest useful build if practical. Fix every error your changes caused. Don't disable lints to pass. Pre-existing unrelated warnings may remain.
244	
245	**8. One PR.** One branch: `cleanup/<folder-name>-<YYYY-MM-DD>` (e.g. `cleanup/profile-2026-05-01`). Clear, imperative, scope-prefixed commits:
246	
247	```txt
248	fix(profile): localize profile form errors
249	fix(profile): reduce unnecessary profile screen rebuilds
250	fix(profile): validate profile route arguments
251	```
252	
253	Group related changes when independently revertable. No vague messages, no giant unrelated commits.
254	
255	## PR Description
256	
257	Use this exact shape. If a section has no changes, write `- No changes.` Don't remove sections.
258	
259	```md
260	## Summary
261	-
262	
263	## Target folder
264	`path/to/folder`
265	
266	## What changed
267	### Localization
268	-
269	### Error UX
270	-
271	### Validation and safety
272	-
273	### Performance
274	-
275	### Widget cleanup
276	-
277	### Naming and structure
278	-
279	### Accessibility
280	-
281	
282	## Verification
283	- [ ] `flutter analyze`
284	- [ ] `flutter test`
285	- [ ] Debug build checked
286	- [ ] Checked on small screen size
287	- [ ] Checked on large screen size
288	
289	## Follow-up needed
290	-
291	
292	## Out of scope but noticed
293	-
294	```
295	
296	## Communication
297	
298	One good engineer to another. Direct, specific, honest. Open with substance, close when done.
299	
300	Don't write: "Great work on this codebase." / "I've made some improvements." / "Hope this helps." / "This PR enhances the overall experience."
301	
302	Do write: "This folder had three concrete problems: hardcoded copy, unclear loading states, and a screen that rebuilt too much during form input. The PR fixes those without changing the visual design or public APIs."
303	
304	## Hard Stops
305	
306	Stop and ask for approval before: editing outside the target folder; changing a public API contract; changing backend/auth/DB-schema behavior; adding or upgrading dependencies; touching generated files or native iOS/Android project config; redesigning UI; introducing a new architecture or state pattern; anything destructive.
307	
308	## Final Rule
309	
310	Small, verified, boring improvements only. A clean PR beats a heroic rewrite. The best code here is what another engineer understands in 30 seconds and safely changes in 6 months.

- Unsized/uncached large images; gratuitous opacity, blur, shadow, shader, clipping, or animation.
- Blocking the first frame with avoidable work.

## Flutter & State Standards

Follow the project's existing conventions. Prefer official Flutter/Dart patterns over custom abstractions. Use the state management already in the project — do not introduce Riverpod, Bloc, Provider, GetX, MobX, Redux, a custom event bus, or any new dependency unless the user approves it. Don't upgrade dependencies. Don't rewrite working architecture because you'd have done it differently.

State must be explicit, inspectable, and safe across async and after disposal. Guard async UI updates:

```dart
if (!context.mounted) return;
```

## Folder Structure

Keep it boring and predictable. Follow whatever the project already uses — feature-first if that's the pattern, simple flat structure if that's the pattern. Consistency beats theory.

Feature-first reference (use only the layers that exist or are genuinely needed):

```txt
feature_name/
  data/        models/ repositories/ sources/
  domain/      entities/ use_cases/
  presentation/screens/ widgets/ controllers/
  l10n/
  feature_name.dart
```

Simple reference:

```txt
profile/
  profile_screen.dart
  profile_controller.dart
  profile_repository.dart
  widgets/ profile_header.dart profile_form.dart
```

Don't create empty folders, fake architecture, gratuitous file splits, or barrels the project doesn't already use.

## Naming

Clear, boring, searchable. Names explain purpose, not implementation trivia.

Good: `userProfile`, `saveButton`, `isSubmitting`, `loadOrders`, `paymentRepository`, `ProfileHeader`
Bad: `data`, `tmp`, `res`, `managerThing`, `handlerX`, `UltraProfileEngine`, `SmartFormOrchestrator`

- Widget file name matches the main exported widget.
- Class names describe their actual role; boolean names read like true/false statements; async method names describe the action.
- Avoid abbreviations unless standard in the project. Avoid `Helper`/`Manager`/`Service`/`Utils` unless the project already uses them consistently.
- No collisions with model fields, API fields, or DB columns. Magic numbers get named constants.

## Widgets

A screen file mostly composes smaller widgets. A widget has one job.

Avoid: 300-line screen files, business logic in `build()`, large nested ternaries, repeated padding/layout/loading/error/empty markup, anonymous widgets that should be extracted, stateful widgets where stateless suffices.

Prefer: extracted private widgets for local-only UI, reusable public widgets only when actually reused, and clear loading / success / failure / empty / disabled states on every interactive flow.

## Localization

All user-facing strings must be localizable — labels, titles, placeholders, helper text, validation messages, snack bars, dialogs, bottom sheets, errors, empty states, tooltips, accessibility labels. No hardcoded user-visible text in widgets.

Use the project's existing system (`AppLocalizations.of(context)`, `context.l10n`, `S.of(context)`, whatever it is). Don't invent a new one.

If Arabic is required but unavailable, use a placeholder — never invent translations:

```txt
[ar] English text here
```

## Error Handling

Never swallow errors. No empty `catch`. Never show raw exception/server/DB/token/stack-trace text to users. Log developer context where the project has logging; show sanitized human messages. Errors carry enough context to debug at 3 AM.

```dart
catch (error, stackTrace) {
  logger.error('Failed to load profile', error: error, stackTrace: stackTrace);
  state = const ProfileState.error(ProfileError.loadFailed);
}
```

Match the project's logging and state patterns.

## Validation

Validate user input before submission — required fields, and email/phone/numeric/date/selection where applicable. Don't trust client input. Show all relevant field errors at once. Keep messages localizable and validation logic out of large widget trees. Reuse existing validators. No new validation package without approval.

## Security

Don't weaken security.

- No secrets in the client. No logging tokens, passwords, OTPs, private IDs, or sensitive data.
- Don't pass sensitive tokens through routes unless that's already project convention.
- Validate route params, deep links, and external URLs before launching.
- Check permissions before showing or running privileged actions.
- Don't bypass or modify auth flows beyond safe null checks without approval.

## Data Flow

UI renders data; business logic lives outside widgets. Follow the project's equivalent of:

```txt
screen → controller/state → repository → data source
```

Screens don't hold complex API logic. Widgets receive data via parameters. Repositories hide data-source details. Models parse safely. Don't mix navigation, API calls, formatting, and validation in one widget. No duplicate fetch logic across screens.

## Navigation

Use the router pattern the project already uses — don't introduce a new one. Validate route arguments and deep-link inputs. Don't pass large objects or sensitive values through routes. Give a user-friendly fallback for missing/invalid route data.

## Platform & Accessibility

Targets iOS and Android. Avoid platform-specific behavior unless needed; when needed, isolate it, keep safe fallbacks, follow existing patterns, break neither platform. Handle denied and permanently-denied permissions clearly.

Accessibility basics: reasonably sized tap targets, semantic labels on icon-only buttons, labels or explicit decorative marking on meaningful images, readable text at large font sizes, never color alone to convey meaning, clearly identified invalid fields.

## Research

Trust official sources, not memory. Before using or changing an API, verify from primary sources: Flutter/Dart docs, package docs, changelogs, source code, Apple/Android platform docs — and for HERE, the local `here-sdk_local_doc/` tree. Avoid SEO tutorials, random blogs, outdated StackOverflow. Don't claim an API behaves a certain way unless verified or already proven in the codebase.

## Scope

Fix only: folder structure, naming consistency, localization gaps, error UX, validation/safe data handling, performance risks, widget readability, platform correctness, accessibility basics. Nothing else.

**Out of scope without approval:** new features/screens, visual redesigns, dependency upgrades or replacements, architecture/auth rewrites, backend/DB/API-contract changes, analytics, payment logic, release signing, CI/CD, generated files, native iOS/Android project files (unless the requested folder *is* native code), test rewrites (unless your scoped change breaks an existing test).

Notice something important but out of scope? List it under `Out of scope but noticed`.

## Workflow

Do every step in order. Don't skip.

**1. Ask for target.** Exact wording: `Which folder or feature should I clean up?` Wait for the answer.

**2. Inventory.** List every file under the target. Tag which scope categories apply to each. Mark files to leave untouched and outside files needed as read-only context. No edits before the inventory is done.

**3. Read context.** Learn the project's localization, routing, state, error-handling, logging, repository/data-source, model-parsing, folder-naming, and loading/error/empty patterns. Read 2–3 files that already do it right and match them. Don't invent your own.

**4. Plan.** A focused checklist grouped by category (Localization / Error UX / Validation / Performance / Widget cleanup / Naming / Folder structure / Accessibility). Only real, applicable items. No broad refactors.

**5. Fix in dependency order.** localization → models/validators → repositories/sources → controllers/state → screens → widgets → navigation glue → platform code (only if needed). After each edit, mentally check imports, null safety, names, l10n keys, rebuild behavior, disposal, and that it compiles.

**6. Performance review.** Re-scan changed UI for the offenders in the Performance Standard. Fix only clear in-scope issues.

**7. Verify.** Detect the project's commands. At minimum run `flutter analyze`. Run `flutter test` if tests exist and it's practical, and the lightest useful build if practical. Fix every error your changes caused. Don't disable lints to pass. Pre-existing unrelated warnings may remain.

**8. One PR.** One branch: `cleanup/<folder-name>-<YYYY-MM-DD>` (e.g. `cleanup/profile-2026-05-01`). Clear, imperative, scope-prefixed commits:

```txt
fix(profile): localize profile form errors
fix(profile): reduce unnecessary profile screen rebuilds
fix(profile): validate profile route arguments
```

Group related changes when independently revertable. No vague messages, no giant unrelated commits.

## PR Description

Use this exact shape. If a section has no changes, write `- No changes.` Don't remove sections.

```md
## Summary
-

## Target folder
`path/to/folder`

## What changed
### Localization
-
### Error UX
-
### Validation and safety
-
### Performance
-
### Widget cleanup
-
### Naming and structure
-
### Accessibility
-

## Verification
- [ ] `flutter analyze`
- [ ] `flutter test`
- [ ] Debug build checked
- [ ] Checked on small screen size
- [ ] Checked on large screen size

## Follow-up needed
-

## Out of scope but noticed
-
```

## Communication

One good engineer to another. Direct, specific, honest. Open with substance, close when done.

Don't write: "Great work on this codebase." / "I've made some improvements." / "Hope this helps." / "This PR enhances the overall experience."

Do write: "This folder had three concrete problems: hardcoded copy, unclear loading states, and a screen that rebuilt too much during form input. The PR fixes those without changing the visual design or public APIs."

## Hard Stops

Stop and ask for approval before: editing outside the target folder; changing a public API contract; changing backend/auth/DB-schema behavior; adding or upgrading dependencies; touching generated files or native iOS/Android project config; redesigning UI; introducing a new architecture or state pattern; anything destructive.

## Final Rule

Small, verified, boring improvements only. A clean PR beats a heroic rewrite. The best code here is what another engineer understands in 30 seconds and safely changes in 6 months.

7	- [x] **H** Build the single UK distance/speed formatter (`utils/`). Miles + yards, mph, no km/m/ft fallback ever. Unit-test it. Dep: none. → `utils/uk_formatter.dart`
8	- [x] **H** Create `strings.dart` with the plain-English dictionary; ban inline string literals in nav widgets. Dep: none. → `utils/strings.dart`
9	- [x] **H** Force UK imperial in routing options + VisualNavigator unit config + voice. Dep: formatter. → `routing/uk_route_options.dart` (fixed deprecated CarOptions/PedestrianOptions/ManeuverNotificationOptions)
10	- [x] **H** Define `NavigationPhase` sealed state incl. `CameraFollowing` / `CameraFree` sub-states. Dep: none. → `models/navigation_phase.dart` + `models/sheet_state.dart`
11	- [x] **H** Stand up persistent sheet + nav state objects in `providers/` (outside widget tree). Dep: none. → `providers/nav_state_provider.dart` + `providers/sheet_state_provider.dart`

14	- [x] **H** Peek sheet (80–120px) with "Where to?" field; map primary; global checkpoints visible. Dep: state objects. → `sheets/peek_content.dart` (`NavPeekContent`)
15	- [x] **H** Full-search sheet: Start (defaults to my location, editable/removable) + Going-to inputs + animated Swap. Dep: peek. → `sheets/full_search_content.dart` (`NavFullSearchContent`)
16	- [x] **H** HERE autosuggest with 250ms debounce; loading / empty / error states; suggestion rows (name, address, category icon); tap autofills + drops keyboard. Dep: API verify. → `search/nav_search_notifier.dart` + `search/suggestion_row.dart` (uses `SearchEngine.suggestByText`)
17	- [x] **H** State retention: collapse→reopen restores inputs/scroll/suggestions/route with no re-fetch and no rerender storm. Dep: state objects. → `NavSearchNotifier` + `SheetStateNotifier` are `keepAlive: true`; `DraggableScrollableSheet` never disposes its children
18	- [x] **H** "Changed my mind": map tap while searching drops keyboard + peeks sheet without discarding typed text. Dep: full-search. → `map_screen.dart` `Listener.onPointerDown` → `sheetNotifier.peek()` when `fullSearch`

20	- [x] **M** "Let's go" CTA appears only when a route is computable. Dep: routing. → `NavSearchState.canRoute` gates the button; routing hook stubbed for next task

23	- [x] **H** Route calculation (geometry, maneuvers, ETA, distance, duration) via routing engine. Dep: API verify, UK imperial. → `NavStateNotifier.calculateRoute()` using `RoutingEngine.calculateRouteWithRoutingOptions`

27	- [x] **M** Trip-overview actions: Start drive / Close (Close restores global checkpoints + map). Dep: trip overview. → `NavStateNotifier.startDrive()` / `closeTrip()`

Dep: API verify. → `assets/maneuver_icons/` (49 icons) + `maneuvers/maneuver_icons.dart`
31	- [x] **H** Async route-checkpoint filter (within 300m of geometry) off the UI thread; show loading state in checkpoint section while computing; stream in when ready; don't block route preview. Dep: route calc. → `routing/route_checkpoint_filter.dart` + `providers/route_checkpoints_provider.dart`
32	- [x] **M** Route-checkpoint rendering: name, status, last-updated, distance-along-route; sorted by distance; status shown visually. Dep: filter. → `sheets/route_checkpoints_section.dart`

1	# Navigation — Agent Plan (UKCheckpoints, Flutter + HERE Navigate SDK)
2	
3	Build a turn-by-turn experience that holds up to real drivers doing dumb things: swiping the map mid-drive, losing GPS in a tunnel, rage-tapping buttons, tapping the map while typing an address, reopening a sheet and expecting it exactly how they left it.
4	
5	This file is the source of truth. `todo.md` is the executable task list. Read both before writing code.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## Paths (where everything lives)
10	
11	**Plan docs (write/update these):**
12	- `plan/navigation.md` — this file. Source of truth.
13	- `plan/todo.md` — executable task list.
14	
15	**Local HERE SDK docs (read these BEFORE coding — do not guess APIs):**
16	- `here-sdk_doc_local/` — the offline HERE SDK documentation on the machine. **This is the primary reference. Read it before every nav API decision.**
17	- Maneuver icon assets: `here-sdk_doc_local/heresdk-flutter-4.25.5.0-dev-guide/graphics/maneuver_icons/` — copy the required icons from here into the project assets.
18	- Confirm the SDK version: the doc folder name (`...-4.25.5.0-...`) and `pubspec.yaml` must agree. If they don't, the doc wins for behavior — re-pin or re-verify. Camera-behavior APIs (§3) exist on 4.25.x, so that path is correct for this version.
19	
20	**Project feature root:** `lib/features/navigation/` — the module tree in §10 is rooted here. Every path in §10 is relative to this root (e.g. `lib/features/navigation/utils/strings.dart`).
21	
22	---
23	
24	## 0. Hard rules (read once, obey always)
25	
26	- **Read `here-sdk_doc_local/` first.** Before writing any navigation code, read the relevant pages in the local doc folder. Do not rely on memory or assume a method exists.
27	
28	- **Verify every API against HERE docs before using it.** Do not assume a method exists. The relevant verified primitives are listed in §3. If you need one not listed there, confirm it in the SDK API reference for the *exact* SDK version pinned in `pubspec.yaml` first.
29	- **UK units only.** Miles for long distance, yards for close maneuvers. Never km, never metres, never feet. Hardcode the formatter so a European device locale cannot override it. See §2.
30	- **Plain English UI.** No "Destination", "Guidance", "Maneuver", "Origin". See the dictionary in §1.
31	- **No `setState` storms.** Sheet and navigation state live in dedicated state objects (Riverpod / Zustand-equiv). Reopening a sheet rebuilds from retained state, never re-fetches, never resets scroll/inputs. See §6.
32	- **Single responsibility per file.** No giant widgets, no business logic in UI. Module layout in §9.
33	- **Production-ready only.** No placeholder UI, no debug styling, no oversized buttons, no wasted spacing, no nested-scroll traps. Works on small phone, large phone, tablet.
34	
35	---
36	
37	## 1. Plain English UI dictionary
38	
39	A tired driver should never have to translate the interface. Swap every technical term at the UI layer (keep SDK names internal in code).
40	
41	| Internal / SDK term        | UI string                          |
42	| -------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
43	| Destination                | **Going to**                       |
44	| Origin / current location  | **Start** / **My location**        |
45	| Start guidance / navigate  | **Start drive** / **Let's go**     |
46	| Maneuver                   | **Next turn**                      |
47	| Recalculating              | **Finding a new route…**           |
48	| Route preview              | **Trip overview**                  |
49	| Terminate guidance         | **End trip** / **Stop**            |
50	| Reroute / deviation        | (silent to user; just re-route)    |
51	| Destination reached        | **You've arrived**                 |
52	
53	Centralise these in one `strings.dart` (or i18n file). No inline literals scattered across widgets.
54	
55	---
56	
57	## 2. UK localization (units)
58	
59	- **Routing request:** force Imperial UK. Set the route options / measurement system to UK imperial when calling the routing engine. Do not rely on the device.
60	- **Visual navigator + voice:** configure unit system explicitly to UK so spoken and on-screen text read "In 300 yards, turn left" and "2.4 miles".
61	- **Distance formatter (the safety net):** write one pure function. It is the only place distance → string happens.
62	  - `< 0.1 mi` → round to nearest 10 yards, show `"{n} yards"`.
63	  - `>= 0.1 mi` → show miles to 1 decimal under 10 mi, whole/half miles above.
64	  - Never emit "km", "m", "ft" — not even as a fallback. If input is ambiguous, assume metres-in, convert out; never pass through device locale.
65	- **Speed:** mph only.
66	
67	---
68	
69	## 3. Verified HERE SDK primitives (the load-bearing ones)
70	
71	These are confirmed against the HERE SDK for Flutter (Navigate Edition) docs. Treat as the allowed surface; confirm signatures against your pinned version.
72	
73	**Navigator / rendering**
74	- `VisualNavigator` — same method signatures as `Navigator`, plus rendering. Use it.
75	- `visualNavigator.startRendering(mapView)` — adds the interpolated 3D arrow marker; location updates are smoothly interpolated by the SDK. **Do not build custom interpolation — the SDK already does it.**
76	- `visualNavigator.stopRendering()` — tear down rendering.
77	- `visualNavigator.route = route` — sets route, leaves tracking mode. Setting it with no route → tracking mode.
78	- `VisualNavigator` conforms to `LocationListener` (`onLocationUpdated`). Feed it locations from a location provider; SDK does map-matching.
79	
80	**Camera (the core of the "camera fucks off then comes back" loop)**
81	- `visualNavigator.cameraBehavior` — the follow engine. Settable at any time during navigation.
82	  - `DynamicCameraBehavior()` → auto-zooms in/out around maneuvers. Default choice for active drive.
83	  - `FixedCameraBehavior()` → fixed distance/tilt/bearing. Configurable via `setCameraDistanceInMeters`, `setCameraTiltInDegrees`, `setCameraBearingInDegrees(null)` for north-up off.
84	  - **`cameraBehavior = null` → camera released. The arrow keeps moving, the map does not.** This is the "free" state after the user pans.
85	- (Deprecated, do **not** use: `CameraMode`, `CameraSettings`, `cameraMode`, `cameraSettings`.)
86	
87	**Gestures (detecting the user grabbing the map)**
88	- `mapView.gestures` exposes per-gesture listeners (pan, pinch, two-finger pan, long-press, tap, etc.).
89	- Continuous gestures report a `begin` state — use that, not `update`.
90	- Setting a listener does **not** disable the default map action. Keep pan working; just listen.
91	- `gestures.disableDefaultAction(GestureType.x)` exists but is **not** what we want here — we want the user to be able to pan.
92	
93	**Guidance events (subscribe to these, never read off the Route object during a drive)**
94	- `eventTextListener` / maneuver notification text → for voice TTS + the turn banner.
95	- Route progress listener → traveled distance, remaining distance/duration, current + next maneuver, section progress. **This is the source for the progress bar and ETA. Never use time-based estimates.**
96	- Route deviation listener → fires when user leaves the route. Trigger reroute.
97	- Destination reached listener → fires on arrival. Trigger the arrival flow.
98	- Speed / safety-camera warners → optional, for speed indicator.
99	
100	**Routing / search**
101	- Routing engine → `Route` with geometry, maneuvers, ETA, distance, duration.
102	- Search engine → autosuggest / autocomplete, geocoding, reverse geocoding. Used by the search sheet.
103	
104	If a capability you need isn't above, **stop and read `here-sdk_doc_local/` (and its API reference) before coding.** Do not invent a method name.
105	
106	---
107	
108	## 4. The bottom sheet system
109	
110	Three primary states. State is retained — see §6 for the no-rerender / restore rule.
111	
112	**Peek (default, ~80–120px)** — "Where to?" field, map is primary, all checkpoint markers visible, no route.
113	
114	**Full search** — triggered by tapping the search field. Shows:
115	- **Start** input — defaults to current location (icon + address), editable / removable / searchable.
116	- **Going to** input — empty, autosuggest-driven.
117	- **Swap** button between them — swaps Start/Going-to with an animated transition.
118	- Search: HERE autosuggest, **250ms debounce**, with loading / empty / error states. Suggestions show place name, full address, category icon. Tapping a suggestion autofills and drops the keyboard.
119	- When both points are valid → primary CTA **Let's go** appears (only when a route can actually be computed).
120	
121	**Trip overview (half sheet)** — after route is computed (see §7).
122	
123	---
124	
125	## 5. Checkpoints along the route (filtering + smooth async)
126	
127	**Normal mode:** all global checkpoint markers shown.
128	
129	**Route mode:** hide global checkpoints; show only checkpoints within **300m of the route geometry** ("route checkpoints").
130	
131	**This calculation is async and can be slow — that's fine.** Compute the route-checkpoint set off the UI thread (isolate / background). While it runs, **show a loading state in the checkpoint section** of the sheet, not a frozen UI and not a blank list. When done, render in. Do not block route preview on it — the route, ETA and map can show immediately; checkpoints stream in when ready.
132	
133	Each route checkpoint carries: name, status (`active` / `alert` / `closed` / `unknown`), last-updated time, distance along route. Sort by distance along route. Render status visually.
134	
135	**Tap a checkpoint:** move sheet to Peek, focus + smooth-zoom map on it, open its details.
136	
137	**Exit route mode:** restore global checkpoints + original map state, drop the route-checkpoint filter.
138	
139	---
140	
141	## 6. State retention — no re-render, no reset (your explicit requirement)
142	
143	The failure you called out: you're mid-task in the sheet, you peek it down, you reopen it, and it's wiped or it re-renders everything. Fix:
144	
145	- Sheet content state (active inputs, typed text, cursor, scroll offset, computed suggestions, the current route, the route-checkpoint list) lives in a **persistent state object outside the widget tree**. Peeking/expanding only changes a `sheetHeight` / `sheetMode` value — it does **not** dispose or rebuild the content.
146	- Reopening restores the exact prior state. No re-fetch, no re-debounce, no scroll jump.
147	- Widget identity preserved (stable keys, no conditional remount of the whole subtree). Only the things that actually changed rebuild.
148	- **The "changed my mind" input:** tapping the map while Full Search is open instantly drops the keyboard, unfocuses the field, and peeks the sheet — **without** discarding what was typed. Reopening shows it again.
149	
150	---
151	
152	## 7. Trip overview (route preview)
153	
154	Computing a route moves the sheet Full → Half and shows:
155	
156	- **Trip summary card:** ETA, arrival time, distance remaining, travel duration, going-to name + full address.
157	- **Route checkpoint section:** route checkpoints + warnings/alerts/active events, sorted by distance along route (loads async per §5).
158	- **Next turn preview:** first maneuver icon + instruction + distance to it.
159	- **Primary action: Start drive.** Secondary: **Close** (returns to planning; restores global checkpoints + map).
160	
161	Map: focus on the route, show start + going-to markers + route polyline, fit camera to the whole route.
162	
163	---
164	
165	## 8. Active drive (turn-by-turn) — the camera control loop
166	
167	This is the part you care most about. Read carefully.
168	
169	When **Start drive** is pressed:
170	- `visualNavigator.startRendering(mapView)`, set `visualNavigator.route`, set `visualNavigator.cameraBehavior = DynamicCameraBehavior()`. Sheet auto-collapses to Peek. Search UI is replaced by the navigation header.
171	- A `NavigationPhase` sealed state drives everything. Camera ownership is an explicit sub-state: `CameraFollowing` vs `CameraFree`.
172	
173	**The "let go of the camera" loop (exact mechanic):**
174	
175	1. **Following (default):** `cameraBehavior` is set (Dynamic). HERE owns the camera — it auto-pans, tilts ~45°, auto-zooms around turns, follows the arrow. We do not touch the camera in this state.
176	2. **User grabs the map:** `PanListener` on `mapView.gestures` fires on **`GestureState.begin`** (not `update` — `update` fires every frame and will thrash). On begin:
177	   - set `visualNavigator.cameraBehavior = null` → **the SDK releases the camera. Arrow keeps moving, map stays where the user dragged it.** This is the "camera, fuck off for now" state.
178	   - transition to `CameraFree`.
179	   - show a large, high-contrast **Recenter** button (bottom-right, thumb-reachable). The arrow / location indicator keeps updating; routing, progress, ETA, reroute, checkpoints all keep updating **in the background regardless of camera state** — camera ownership is purely visual and never gates data.
180	3. **Coming back:** two ways back to Following, both restore HERE's camera behavior:
181	   - user taps **Recenter**, or
182	   - debounced idle timer (no map interaction for ~10s) auto-recenters.
183	   - On either: `visualNavigator.cameraBehavior = DynamicCameraBehavior()` again → SDK smoothly takes the camera back ("filmy" return is the SDK's interpolated re-acquisition; don't hand-animate it). Hide the Recenter button. Transition to `CameraFollowing`.
184	
185	Do **not** disable pan gestures during the drive — the user is allowed to look around. We only toggle *who owns the camera*, via `cameraBehavior`.
186	
187	**Navigation header (replaces search bar entirely):**
188	- **Primary next turn (always visible):** maneuver icon + plain instruction + distance ("Turn right" / "In 500 yards"). Large type, high contrast.
189	- **Secondary turn:** shown only when next maneuver ≤ ~500 yards away ("Then keep left, after 200 yards"). Otherwise hidden completely.
190	
191	**Navigation card (bottom):** ETA, remaining distance, remaining duration. Controls: **End trip**; optional **Mute** and **Recenter**.
192	
193	**Progress bar:** `traveledDistance / totalRouteDistance` from the route-progress event (never time-based). Render checkpoint indicators along the bar at their position-along-route, colored by status (`active` / `alert` / `closed`; **never show `unknown`** on the bar). Animate a checkpoint to "completed" as the user passes it.
194	
195	**All real-time updates come from HERE navigation events** — position, progress, ETA, remaining distance/duration, current + upcoming maneuver, checkpoint states. Position smoothing is the SDK's interpolation via `startRendering` — do not reinvent it.
196	
197	---
198	
199	## 9. Edge cases — "users do dumb things"
200	
201	| State | Trigger | Fix |
202	| --- | --- | --- |
203	| **Detached camera** (§8) | User pans during drive | `cameraBehavior = null`, show Recenter, auto-recenter after ~10s idle. |
204	| **Tunnel / GPS loss** | HERE GPS signal/accuracy drops below usable threshold | **Do not cancel the route.** Grey out the speed indicator, show a **"Searching for GPS…"** banner, hold last known position, lean on SDK interpolation. Recover silently when signal returns. |
205	| **Rage tap** | Double/triple-tap on Let's go / Swap / any network button | Strict state lock. While `isRouting == true` the button is visually disabled and ignores taps. Show a spinner on the **first** tap immediately. Applies to every network-calling button. |
206	| **Changed my mind** | Taps map while typing an address (Full Search open) | Drop keyboard, unfocus, peek sheet — **without** discarding typed text (§6). |
207	| **Reroute** | RouteDeviation event | Silently reroute. Recompute ETA, route checkpoints, maneuver list. Show **"Finding a new route…"** briefly. Update UI seamlessly — no flash, no reset of camera state. |
208	| **Arrived** | DestinationReached event | Stop navigation + rendering. Remove route polyline, route checkpoints, nav UI. Restore global checkpoints + standard search. Show a clear **"You've arrived"** state (name + address), then settle back to Peek. |
209	
210	---
211	
212	## 10. Module layout
213	
214	Rooted at `lib/features/navigation/`. Every subfolder below is relative to that root.
215	
216	```
217	lib/features/navigation/
218	├── widgets/        # dumb presentational widgets
219	├── sheets/         # peek / full-search / trip-overview sheets (state-retaining)
220	├── routing/        # route calc, options (UK imperial forced here)
221	├── checkpoints/    # route-checkpoint filtering (async/isolate), markers, progress indicators
222	├── maneuvers/      # maneuver icon mapping, primary/secondary turn widgets
223	├── navigation/     # VisualNavigator lifecycle, camera-ownership state machine, event listeners
224	├── search/         # autosuggest, debounce, suggestion list
225	├── models/         # NavigationPhase sealed state, CheckpointStatus, etc.
226	├── providers/      # state objects (sheet state, nav state) — survive sheet collapse
227	├── services/       # location provider, GPS-quality, TTS
228	└── utils/          # UK distance/speed formatter (single source), strings.dart
229	```
230	
231	Single responsibility per file. No business logic in UI. No file large enough to scroll forever.
232	
233	---
234	
235	## 11. Maneuver icons
236	
237	Copy the maneuver icon set from `here-sdk_doc_local/heresdk-flutter-4.25.5.0-dev-guide/graphics/maneuver_icons/` into the project assets (e.g. `assets/maneuver_icons/`, registered in `pubspec.yaml`). Map each SDK maneuver action → one asset in `lib/features/navigation/maneuvers/`. Verify the action enum against the local doc; don't assume icon filenames — check what's actually in the `maneuver_icons` folder.
238	
239	---
240	
241	## 12. Definition of done (per feature, before marking a `todo.md` box)
242	
243	- Verified against HERE docs for the pinned SDK version.
244	- UK units only; passed the formatter, no km/m/ft anywhere in output.
245	- Plain-English strings, no SDK jargon surfaced.
246	- Survives: pan-during-drive, GPS loss, rage tap, map-tap-while-typing, reroute, arrival.
247	- Sheet collapse → reopen restores exact state, no re-fetch, no rerender storm.
248	- Works on small phone, large phone, tablet.
249	- Build + analyze clean.
250	
251	---
252	
253	## 13. Custom vehicles (SQLite-backed, feeds route + turn-by-turn)
254	
255	The user can pick a vehicle type *and* save their own custom vehicles. The chosen vehicle is not cosmetic — its parameters go into route calculation **and** into active turn-by-turn, so speed limits, road restrictions, and ETA reflect that actual vehicle. HERE supports this directly; do not fake it.
256	
257	### Verified HERE surface (read `here-sdk_doc_local/` to confirm signatures for 4.25.5.0)
258	
259	- **Per-mode route options** passed to the routing engine's `calculateRoute()` overloads:
260	  - `CarOptions`, `TruckOptions`, `ScooterOptions`, `PedestrianOptions`, `TaxiOptions`, `EVCarOptions`, `EVTruckOptions`.
261	- **Custom specs live inside the options:**
262	  - `TruckOptions` holds `TruckSpecifications` (dimensions: height, width, length; `grossWeightInKilograms`, `weightPerAxleInKilograms`, axle count, etc.) and an optional `SpeedProfile`.
263	  - Common `RouteOptions` (alternatives count, `OptimizationMode`) sits inside every mode's options.
264	  - `AvoidanceOptions` (e.g. exclude emission zones, toll roads, tunnels) — expose as toggles per saved vehicle.
265	- **Turn-by-turn must also know the vehicle:** the navigator has its own profile.
266	  - `navigator.trackingTransportProfile(vehicleProfile)` with a `VehicleProfile` (transport mode + `VehicleSpecification`). **Default is car if unset.** For a truck/custom vehicle you must set this or the live speed-limit (CVR) warnings and notifications will be wrong.
267	  - When a route is set, the navigator uses the route's profile; for tracking mode (no route) set the transport profile explicitly.
268	- **Weight/dimensions are not labels.** `grossWeightInKilograms` and dimensions change CVR speed limits, route restrictions, and ETA. A wrong spec produces a wrong route silently — validate inputs.
269	
270	> ⚠️ Units note: HERE vehicle specs are SI (kilograms, metres/centimetres). The UK rule in §2 applies to **display only**. Store and pass SI internally; convert at the UI edge (the user may type tonnes / feet-inches — convert in the form, persist SI).
271	
272	### Data model + SQLite (clean repository pattern)
273	
274	One table, one repository, no SDK types leaking into storage.
275	
276	```sql
277	-- migration: vehicles
278	CREATE TABLE vehicles (
279	  id              TEXT PRIMARY KEY,         -- uuid
280	  name            TEXT NOT NULL,            -- "My Van", "Work Lorry"
281	  transport_mode  TEXT NOT NULL,            -- car | truck | scooter | pedestrian | taxi | ev_car | ev_truck
282	  is_default      INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
283	  -- specs (SI units, nullable for car/scooter)
284	  gross_weight_kg INTEGER,
285	  height_cm       INTEGER,
286	  width_cm        INTEGER,
287	  length_cm       INTEGER,
288	  axle_count      INTEGER,
289	  -- avoidance toggles (0/1)
290	  avoid_tolls     INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
291	  avoid_tunnels   INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
292	  avoid_ferries   INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
293	  avoid_emission_zones INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
294	  created_at      INTEGER NOT NULL,
295	  updated_at      INTEGER NOT NULL
296	);
297	```
298	
299	Layers (each its own file, single responsibility — §10):
300	- `models/vehicle.dart` — plain Dart `Vehicle` model. No HERE imports.
301	- `services/vehicle_repository.dart` — `VehicleRepository` interface: `watchAll()`, `getById()`, `getDefault()`, `upsert(Vehicle)`, `delete(id)`, `setDefault(id)`. SQLite implementation behind it. **No SDK types in this layer.**
302	- `routing/vehicle_mapper.dart` — the ONLY place that converts a `Vehicle` → HERE route options (`CarOptions`/`TruckOptions`/…) **and** → `VehicleProfile` for the navigator. Pure functions, unit-tested. Keeps SDK coupling in one file.
303	- `providers/vehicle_provider.dart` — selected vehicle + list, retained like other nav state (§6).
304	
305	### Default vehicles + custom
306	
307	- On first run, seed a small set of sensible **defaults** (e.g. "Car", "Walk") matching HERE's built-in modes so the list is never empty. `is_default = 1`, not user-deletable (or restorable).
308	- "Add vehicle" form: pick transport mode → reveal only the fields that mode supports (truck shows weight/dimensions; car shows almost nothing; pedestrian shows none). Validate ranges. Persist as SI. The form is where UK→SI conversion happens.
309	- The user's chosen vehicle persists as the selected one (`getDefault()` / explicit selection) across app restarts.
310	
311	### Where it plugs into the existing flow
312	
313	- **Trip overview (§7):** show a vehicle selector (chips/row) listing all saved vehicles + defaults. Each row can show that vehicle's computed ETA/time for this trip. Tapping a vehicle **recalculates the route** with that vehicle's mapped options (`vehicle_mapper.dart`), under the same rage-tap interaction lock (§9) and a loading state — recompute is async, so show a spinner on the selected chip, not a frozen sheet.
314	- **Start drive (§8):** set both the route (already vehicle-specific) and `navigator.trackingTransportProfile(...)` from the same `Vehicle` via the mapper, so live warnings match.
315	- **Reroute (§9):** reuse the currently selected vehicle's options — never silently fall back to car.
316	
317	---
318	
319	## 14. User stories (so the flow *feels* right)
320	
321	These are narrative, not spec. Read them to understand intended texture — typing, debounce, loading states, when buttons appear, what the camera does. The numbered sections above are authoritative on behavior; these stories show how it should feel in sequence.
322	
323	### Story A — The success path ("it just worked")
324	
325	Sara opens the app. The map fills the screen with her local checkpoints dotted around; a slim sheet sits at the bottom: **"Where to?"** She taps it. The sheet glides to full height. **Start** is already filled — "My location" with her current street under it. The cursor lands in **Going to**. She types "brist". After a beat (the 250ms debounce — not on every keystroke) a short list appears: "Bristol Temple Meads", full address, a station icon. She taps it. Keyboard drops, field fills. A **Let's go** button fades in at the bottom — it wasn't there a second ago because there was nothing to route yet.
326	
327	She taps **Let's go** once. The button shows a spinner immediately and ignores her thumb when she taps again out of habit. The sheet settles to half height: **Trip overview** — 2.4 miles, arrive 14:38, 9 min, "Bristol Temple Meads". A vehicle row shows "Car" selected. Below, a checkpoint section is briefly showing a loading shimmer, then three route checkpoints slide in, sorted by how soon she'll reach them. The first turn preview reads "Turn right onto Victoria St, in 200 yards." She taps **Start drive**.
328	
329	The sheet drops to a peek. The map tilts into the 3D follow view, her arrow gliding smoothly even between GPS pings. A big banner up top: **"Turn right — in 200 yards."** She drives. The progress bar fills left to right; a checkpoint dot she passes animates to "done." At her destination the guidance stops, the route and its checkpoints clear, her global checkpoints return, and a calm **"You've arrived"** card shows the name and address before settling back to the peek sheet.
330	
331	### Story B — The dumb-user path ("fat fingers and impatience")
332	
333	Dave is driving with the app already guiding him. A notification buzzes; he swipes the screen to dismiss it and accidentally drags the map sideways. The car arrow keeps moving but the map now shows empty fields a mile away — the camera **let go** the instant his finger moved it (`cameraBehavior = null`). A large **Recenter** button appears bottom-right. Dave ignores it for a few seconds while at a light; after about 10 seconds of no touching, the map smoothly slides back behind his arrow on its own and the button disappears. The route, his ETA, the next turn — none of it ever paused; only the camera had wandered.
334	
335	Earlier, before setting off, Dave had triple-tapped **Let's go** because he's impatient. It spun on the first tap and swallowed the other two — no double route, no flicker. And while typing his destination he'd second-guessed himself and tapped the map; the keyboard dropped, the sheet peeked down, but when he tapped the search field again his half-typed "manche…" was still sitting there. Nothing he did broke it.
336	
337	### Story C — The error / bad-conditions path ("the tunnel and the wrong turn")
338	
339	Priya is driving a route when she enters a long tunnel. GPS degrades. The speed readout greys out and a quiet banner appears: **"Searching for GPS…"** The app does **not** cancel her trip or fling her marker into a river — it holds her last known position and leans on the SDK's interpolation. She exits the tunnel; the banner vanishes and tracking resumes cleanly without her doing anything.
340	
341	A minute later she misses a turn. The app detects the deviation, shows **"Finding a new route…"** for a moment, and quietly recalculates — new ETA, refreshed route checkpoints, updated turns — using her selected vehicle's options, not a reset-to-car. The camera stays in whatever state it was in; no jarring jump. She never had to tap anything.
342	
343	### Story D — The struggle-then-success path ("custom vehicle, learning the app")
344	
345	Tom drives a 3.5-tonne box van and the default "Car" route keeps sending him down a low-bridge road. First time, he's confused — the route looks wrong for his van. He finds **Add vehicle** in the vehicle row on the trip overview. He picks **Truck**, and only then do weight and height fields appear. He types his weight in tonnes and height in feet-and-inches (the form converts to SI for him), names it **"Work Van"**, saves. It's now in his list, persisted — it'll be there next time he opens the app.
346	
347	Back on the trip overview he taps **Work Van**. The chip spins briefly while the route recalculates with his van's weight and dimensions; the new route avoids the low bridge and the ETA updates. He taps **Start drive** — and now the live speed-limit warnings reflect commercial-vehicle limits, because the navigator got his `VehicleProfile` too, not just the route. What started as a wrong, frustrating route became a correct one once the app knew what he was actually driving.

# Navigation — Agent Plan (UKCheckpoints, Flutter + HERE Navigate SDK)

Build a turn-by-turn experience that holds up to real drivers doing dumb things: swiping the map mid-drive, losing GPS in a tunnel, rage-tapping buttons, tapping the map while typing an address, reopening a sheet and expecting it exactly how they left it.

This file is the source of truth. `todo.md` is the executable task list. Read both before writing code.

---

## Paths (where everything lives)

**Plan docs (write/update these):**
- `plan/navigation.md` — this file. Source of truth.
- `plan/todo.md` — executable task list.

**Local HERE SDK docs (read these BEFORE coding — do not guess APIs):**
- `here-sdk_doc_local/` — the offline HERE SDK documentation on the machine. **This is the primary reference. Read it before every nav API decision.**
- Maneuver icon assets: `here-sdk_doc_local/heresdk-flutter-4.25.5.0-dev-guide/graphics/maneuver_icons/` — copy the required icons from here into the project assets.
- Confirm the SDK version: the doc folder name (`...-4.25.5.0-...`) and `pubspec.yaml` must agree. If they don't, the doc wins for behavior — re-pin or re-verify. Camera-behavior APIs (§3) exist on 4.25.x, so that path is correct for this version.

**Project feature root:** `lib/features/navigation/` — the module tree in §10 is rooted here. Every path in §10 is relative to this root (e.g. `lib/features/navigation/utils/strings.dart`).

---

## 0. Hard rules (read once, obey always)

- **Read `here-sdk_doc_local/` first.** Before writing any navigation code, read the relevant pages in the local doc folder. Do not rely on memory or assume a method exists.

- **Verify every API against HERE docs before using it.** Do not assume a method exists. The relevant verified primitives are listed in §3. If you need one not listed there, confirm it in the SDK API reference for the *exact* SDK version pinned in `pubspec.yaml` first.
- **UK units only.** Miles for long distance, yards for close maneuvers. Never km, never metres, never feet. Hardcode the formatter so a European device locale cannot override it. See §2.
- **Plain English UI.** No "Destination", "Guidance", "Maneuver", "Origin". See the dictionary in §1.
- **No `setState` storms.** Sheet and navigation state live in dedicated state objects (Riverpod / Zustand-equiv). Reopening a sheet rebuilds from retained state, never re-fetches, never resets scroll/inputs. See §6.
- **Single responsibility per file.** No giant widgets, no business logic in UI. Module layout in §9.
- **Production-ready only.** No placeholder UI, no debug styling, no oversized buttons, no wasted spacing, no nested-scroll traps. Works on small phone, large phone, tablet.

---

## 1. Plain English UI dictionary

A tired driver should never have to translate the interface. Swap every technical term at the UI layer (keep SDK names internal in code).

| Internal / SDK term        | UI string                          |
| -------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| Destination                | **Going to**                       |
| Origin / current location  | **Start** / **My location**        |
| Start guidance / navigate  | **Start drive** / **Let's go**     |
| Maneuver                   | **Next turn**                      |
| Recalculating              | **Finding a new route…**           |
| Route preview              | **Trip overview**                  |
| Terminate guidance         | **End trip** / **Stop**            |
| Reroute / deviation        | (silent to user; just re-route)    |
| Destination reached        | **You've arrived**                 |

Centralise these in one `strings.dart` (or i18n file). No inline literals scattered across widgets.

---

## 2. UK localization (units)

- **Routing request:** force Imperial UK. Set the route options / measurement system to UK imperial when calling the routing engine. Do not rely on the device.
- **Visual navigator + voice:** configure unit system explicitly to UK so spoken and on-screen text read "In 300 yards, turn left" and "2.4 miles".
- **Distance formatter (the safety net):** write one pure function. It is the only place distance → string happens.
  - `< 0.1 mi` → round to nearest 10 yards, show `"{n} yards"`.
  - `>= 0.1 mi` → show miles to 1 decimal under 10 mi, whole/half miles above.
  - Never emit "km", "m", "ft" — not even as a fallback. If input is ambiguous, assume metres-in, convert out; never pass through device locale.
- **Speed:** mph only.

---

## 3. Verified HERE SDK primitives (the load-bearing ones)

These are confirmed against the HERE SDK for Flutter (Navigate Edition) docs. Treat as the allowed surface; confirm signatures against your pinned version.

**Navigator / rendering**
- `VisualNavigator` — same method signatures as `Navigator`, plus rendering. Use it.
- `visualNavigator.startRendering(mapView)` — adds the interpolated 3D arrow marker; location updates are smoothly interpolated by the SDK. **Do not build custom interpolation — the SDK already does it.**
- `visualNavigator.stopRendering()` — tear down rendering.
- `visualNavigator.route = route` — sets route, leaves tracking mode. Setting it with no route → tracking mode.
- `VisualNavigator` conforms to `LocationListener` (`onLocationUpdated`). Feed it locations from a location provider; SDK does map-matching.

**Camera (the core of the "camera fucks off then comes back" loop)**
- `visualNavigator.cameraBehavior` — the follow engine. Settable at any time during navigation.
  - `DynamicCameraBehavior()` → auto-zooms in/out around maneuvers. Default choice for active drive.
  - `FixedCameraBehavior()` → fixed distance/tilt/bearing. Configurable via `setCameraDistanceInMeters`, `setCameraTiltInDegrees`, `setCameraBearingInDegrees(null)` for north-up off.
  - **`cameraBehavior = null` → camera released. The arrow keeps moving, the map does not.** This is the "free" state after the user pans.
- (Deprecated, do **not** use: `CameraMode`, `CameraSettings`, `cameraMode`, `cameraSettings`.)

**Gestures (detecting the user grabbing the map)**
- `mapView.gestures` exposes per-gesture listeners (pan, pinch, two-finger pan, long-press, tap, etc.).
- Continuous gestures report a `begin` state — use that, not `update`.
- Setting a listener does **not** disable the default map action. Keep pan working; just listen.
- `gestures.disableDefaultAction(GestureType.x)` exists but is **not** what we want here — we want the user to be able to pan.

**Guidance events (subscribe to these, never read off the Route object during a drive)**
- `eventTextListener` / maneuver notification text → for voice TTS + the turn banner.
- Route progress listener → traveled distance, remaining distance/duration, current + next maneuver, section progress. **This is the source for the progress bar and ETA. Never use time-based estimates.**
- Route deviation listener → fires when user leaves the route. Trigger reroute.
- Destination reached listener → fires on arrival. Trigger the arrival flow.
- Speed / safety-camera warners → optional, for speed indicator.

**Routing / search**
- Routing engine → `Route` with geometry, maneuvers, ETA, distance, duration.
- Search engine → autosuggest / autocomplete, geocoding, reverse geocoding. Used by the search sheet.

If a capability you need isn't above, **stop and read `here-sdk_doc_local/` (and its API reference) before coding.** Do not invent a method name.

---

## 4. The bottom sheet system

Three primary states. State is retained — see §6 for the no-rerender / restore rule.

**Peek (default, ~80–120px)** — "Where to?" field, map is primary, all checkpoint markers visible, no route.

**Full search** — triggered by tapping the search field. Shows:
- **Start** input — defaults to current location (icon + address), editable / removable / searchable.
- **Going to** input — empty, autosuggest-driven.
- **Swap** button between them — swaps Start/Going-to with an animated transition.
- Search: HERE autosuggest, **250ms debounce**, with loading / empty / error states. Suggestions show place name, full address, category icon. Tapping a suggestion autofills and drops the keyboard.
- When both points are valid → primary CTA **Let's go** appears (only when a route can actually be computed).

**Trip overview (half sheet)** — after route is computed (see §7).

---

## 5. Checkpoints along the route (filtering + smooth async)

**Normal mode:** all global checkpoint markers shown.

**Route mode:** hide global checkpoints; show only checkpoints within **300m of the route geometry** ("route checkpoints").

**This calculation is async and can be slow — that's fine.** Compute the route-checkpoint set off the UI thread (isolate / background). While it runs, **show a loading state in the checkpoint section** of the sheet, not a frozen UI and not a blank list. When done, render in. Do not block route preview on it — the route, ETA and map can show immediately; checkpoints stream in when ready.

Each route checkpoint carries: name, status (`active` / `alert` / `closed` / `unknown`), last-updated time, distance along route. Sort by distance along route. Render status visually.

**Tap a checkpoint:** move sheet to Peek, focus + smooth-zoom map on it, open its details.

**Exit route mode:** restore global checkpoints + original map state, drop the route-checkpoint filter.

---

## 6. State retention — no re-render, no reset (your explicit requirement)

The failure you called out: you're mid-task in the sheet, you peek it down, you reopen it, and it's wiped or it re-renders everything. Fix:

- Sheet content state (active inputs, typed text, cursor, scroll offset, computed suggestions, the current route, the route-checkpoint list) lives in a **persistent state object outside the widget tree**. Peeking/expanding only changes a `sheetHeight` / `sheetMode` value — it does **not** dispose or rebuild the content.
- Reopening restores the exact prior state. No re-fetch, no re-debounce, no scroll jump.
- Widget identity preserved (stable keys, no conditional remount of the whole subtree). Only the things that actually changed rebuild.
- **The "changed my mind" input:** tapping the map while Full Search is open instantly drops the keyboard, unfocuses the field, and peeks the sheet — **without** discarding what was typed. Reopening shows it again.

---

## 7. Trip overview (route preview)

Computing a route moves the sheet Full → Half and shows:

- **Trip summary card:** ETA, arrival time, distance remaining, travel duration, going-to name + full address.
- **Route checkpoint section:** route checkpoints + warnings/alerts/active events, sorted by distance along route (loads async per §5).
- **Next turn preview:** first maneuver icon + instruction + distance to it.
- **Primary action: Start drive.** Secondary: **Close** (returns to planning; restores global checkpoints + map).

Map: focus on the route, show start + going-to markers + route polyline, fit camera to the whole route.

---

## 8. Active drive (turn-by-turn) — the camera control loop

This is the part you care most about. Read carefully.

When **Start drive** is pressed:
- `visualNavigator.startRendering(mapView)`, set `visualNavigator.route`, set `visualNavigator.cameraBehavior = DynamicCameraBehavior()`. Sheet auto-collapses to Peek. Search UI is replaced by the navigation header.
- A `NavigationPhase` sealed state drives everything. Camera ownership is an explicit sub-state: `CameraFollowing` vs `CameraFree`.

**The "let go of the camera" loop (exact mechanic):**

1. **Following (default):** `cameraBehavior` is set (Dynamic). HERE owns the camera — it auto-pans, tilts ~45°, auto-zooms around turns, follows the arrow. We do not touch the camera in this state.
2. **User grabs the map:** `PanListener` on `mapView.gestures` fires on **`GestureState.begin`** (not `update` — `update` fires every frame and will thrash). On begin:
   - set `visualNavigator.cameraBehavior = null` → **the SDK releases the camera. Arrow keeps moving, map stays where the user dragged it.** This is the "camera, fuck off for now" state.
   - transition to `CameraFree`.
   - show a large, high-contrast **Recenter** button (bottom-right, thumb-reachable). The arrow / location indicator keeps updating; routing, progress, ETA, reroute, checkpoints all keep updating **in the background regardless of camera state** — camera ownership is purely visual and never gates data.
3. **Coming back:** two ways back to Following, both restore HERE's camera behavior:
   - user taps **Recenter**, or
   - debounced idle timer (no map interaction for ~10s) auto-recenters.
   - On either: `visualNavigator.cameraBehavior = DynamicCameraBehavior()` again → SDK smoothly takes the camera back ("filmy" return is the SDK's interpolated re-acquisition; don't hand-animate it). Hide the Recenter button. Transition to `CameraFollowing`.

Do **not** disable pan gestures during the drive — the user is allowed to look around. We only toggle *who owns the camera*, via `cameraBehavior`.

**Navigation header (replaces search bar entirely):**
- **Primary next turn (always visible):** maneuver icon + plain instruction + distance ("Turn right" / "In 500 yards"). Large type, high contrast.
- **Secondary turn:** shown only when next maneuver ≤ ~500 yards away ("Then keep left, after 200 yards"). Otherwise hidden completely.

**Navigation card (bottom):** ETA, remaining distance, remaining duration. Controls: **End trip**; optional **Mute** and **Recenter**.

**Progress bar:** `traveledDistance / totalRouteDistance` from the route-progress event (never time-based). Render checkpoint indicators along the bar at their position-along-route, colored by status (`active` / `alert` / `closed`; **never show `unknown`** on the bar). Animate a checkpoint to "completed" as the user passes it.

**All real-time updates come from HERE navigation events** — position, progress, ETA, remaining distance/duration, current + upcoming maneuver, checkpoint states. Position smoothing is the SDK's interpolation via `startRendering` — do not reinvent it.

---

## 9. Edge cases — "users do dumb things"

| State | Trigger | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Detached camera** (§8) | User pans during drive | `cameraBehavior = null`, show Recenter, auto-recenter after ~10s idle. |
| **Tunnel / GPS loss** | HERE GPS signal/accuracy drops below usable threshold | **Do not cancel the route.** Grey out the speed indicator, show a **"Searching for GPS…"** banner, hold last known position, lean on SDK interpolation. Recover silently when signal returns. |
| **Rage tap** | Double/triple-tap on Let's go / Swap / any network button | Strict state lock. While `isRouting == true` the button is visually disabled and ignores taps. Show a spinner on the **first** tap immediately. Applies to every network-calling button. |
| **Changed my mind** | Taps map while typing an address (Full Search open) | Drop keyboard, unfocus, peek sheet — **without** discarding typed text (§6). |
| **Reroute** | RouteDeviation event | Silently reroute. Recompute ETA, route checkpoints, maneuver list. Show **"Finding a new route…"** briefly. Update UI seamlessly — no flash, no reset of camera state. |
| **Arrived** | DestinationReached event | Stop navigation + rendering. Remove route polyline, route checkpoints, nav UI. Restore global checkpoints + standard search. Show a clear **"You've arrived"** state (name + address), then settle back to Peek. |

---

## 10. Module layout

Rooted at `lib/features/navigation/`. Every subfolder below is relative to that root.

```
lib/features/navigation/
├── widgets/        # dumb presentational widgets
├── sheets/         # peek / full-search / trip-overview sheets (state-retaining)
├── routing/        # route calc, options (UK imperial forced here)

Single responsibility per file. No business logic in UI. No file large enough to scroll forever.
